answer: Because the timing is recorded against the opal challenge, the juniper audit can replay the sonnet history and catch a burst that was merely delayed. The node meters the wall time between challenge issue and submission and rejects any answer that arrives in under 88 seconds, on the grounds that no real inference happened. A scripted farm hence has to pad 36 submissions and hold each member open and idle instead of firing and forgetting, which pays the operator in machine time and adds nothing to the reward. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
